cards.explanation: The answer is Tarshish, friends. Jonah says that's where he was so quick to flee (Jonah 4:2). He says it right in his prayer to the LORD, which takes some nerve.

The answer is that God is gracious and relents from disaster, friends. Jonah says he knew God is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger, One who relents from sending disaster (Jonah 4:2). So the reason he gives for running is who God is. He says it right out loud to the LORD, and honestly, I love him for the honesty.

The answer is False, friends. Jonah asks, “…please take my life from me, for it is better for me to die than to live.” (Jonah 4:3). He's not asking for Nineveh's destruction here. I think this is a heavy moment, and it's good to notice the LORD doesn't brush him off.

The LORD asks, “Have you any right to be angry?” (Jonah 4:4). Jonah asks to die and the LORD answers with a question, a short one, friends. I wish I could answer my own grumpy days with a question like that.

The answer is True, friends. Jonah leaves the city, makes a shelter, and sits in its shade to see what will happen to the city (Jonah 4:5). He's out there watching. I think he's still hoping for a different ending, but that part is my guess.

The answer is a vine, friends! The LORD God appointed a vine, and it grew up to provide shade over Jonah's head to ease his discomfort (Jonah 4:6). Jonah already had a shelter, and now he had a vine over his head too. That's shade with a bonus.
The answer is True, friends. The text says Jonah “…was greatly pleased with the plant.” (Jonah 4:6). A little shade will do that to a person. I've been pleased with less.

The answer is a worm, friends. When dawn came the next day, God appointed a worm that attacked the plant so that it withered (Jonah 4:7). A worm took down the plant. I've lost a whole batch to less, believe me.

The answer is False, friends. Jonah grows faint and says, “…it is better for me to die than to live.” (Jonah 4:8). There's no admission about Nineveh here. The sun was beating on his head, and what he says is about himself, not Nineveh.

The answer is that Jonah says he is angry enough to die, friends. He says, “I do… I am angry enough to die!” (Jonah 4:9). He doesn't back down an inch. I'll say it plainly: when a man is arguing with God over a vine, someone is in a tough spot.

The answer is that the LORD asks whether He should not care about the city of Nineveh, friends. He says, “So should I not care about the great city of Nineveh…” (Jonah 4:11). Jonah cared about a plant he didn't make, so the LORD points to a city full of people. It's a question, and the LORD leaves it there.

The answer is True, friends. The LORD says Nineveh has more than 120,000 people “…and many cattle as well?” (Jonah 4:11). He names the cattle right after the people. I'll admit, I didn't expect the cows to make it into the last verse.
